sentences.zh: 嘗自帶綬及冠通天冠，加金附蟬，顧見侍臣武弁上有金蟬，及王公有綬者，竝令去之。

translations.literal: Once, seeing the gold cicada on his own sash and on his Tongtian crown, and the gold cicadas on attending ministers' martial caps, and sashes on kings and dukes, he ordered them all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, seeing the gold cicada on his own sash and on his Tongtian crown, and the gold cicadas on attending ministers' martial caps, and sashes on kings and dukes, he ordered them all removed.

sentences.zh: 又不聽人有高大之稱，諸姓高者改為薑，九族稱高祖者為長祖，曾祖為次長祖，官名凡稱上及大者改為長，有天者亦改之。

translations.literal: He also forbade anyone to use lofty titles; those surnamed Gao were changed to Jiang; the nine kin who called the great-grandfather "high ancestor" called him "chief ancestor," and the grandfather "second chief ancestor"; official titles that used "supreme" or "grand" were changed to "chief," and those with "Heaven" were also changed.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade anyone to use lofty titles; those surnamed Gao were changed to Jiang; the nine kin who called the great-grandfather "high ancestor" called him "chief ancestor," and the grandfather "second chief ancestor"; official titles that used "supreme" or "grand" were changed to "chief," and those with "Heaven" were also changed.

sentences.zh: 又令天下車皆以渾成木為輪，禁天下婦人皆不得施粉黛之飾，唯宮人得乘有輻車，加粉黛焉。

translations.literal: He also ordered that all carriages in the realm use wheels of whole-formed wood, forbade all women in the realm to apply powder and rouge, and allowed only palace women to ride spoke-wheeled carriages and apply powder and rouge.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that all carriages in the realm use wheels of whole-formed wood, forbade all women in the realm to apply powder and rouge, and allowed only palace women to ride spoke-wheeled carriages and apply powder and rouge.

sentences.zh: 西陽公溫，杞國公亮之子，卽帝之從祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Duke of Xiyang Wen was the son of Duke of Qi Yu Liang and the emperor's cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xiyang Wen was the son of Yu Liang, Duke of Qi, and the emperor's cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 其妻尉遲氏有容色，因入朝，帝遂飲之以酒，逼而淫之。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Yuchi was beautiful in appearance; because she entered court, the emperor gave her wine to drink and forced her into licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Yuchi was beautiful in appearance; because she entered court, the emperor gave her wine to drink and forced her into licentiousness.

sentences.zh: 亮聞之，懼誅，乃反。

translations.literal: When Liang heard of it he feared execution and therefore rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang heard of it he feared execution and therefore rebelled.

sentences.zh: 纔誅溫，卽追尉遲氏入宮，初為妃，尋立為皇后。

translations.literal: Hardly had Wen been executed when Lady Yuchi was summoned into the palace; at first she was made consort, and soon afterward was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Wen been executed when Lady Yuchi was summoned into the palace; at first she was made consort, and soon afterward was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 每召侍臣論議，唯欲興造變革，未嘗言及治政。

translations.literal: Whenever he summoned attending ministers to discuss affairs, he wished only to undertake construction and change; he never spoke of governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he summoned attending ministers to discuss affairs, he wished only to undertake construction and change; he never spoke of governing the state.

sentences.zh: 其後遊戲無恆，出入不

translations.literal: Thereafter his pleasures knew no constancy; going out and coming in he showed no
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his pleasures knew no constancy; going out and coming in he showed no

translations.literal: (restraint)
translations.idiomatic: (restraint)

sentences.zh: 〔節〕，羽儀仗衛，晨出夜還。

translations.literal: [decorum]; with guard of honor he went out at dawn and returned at night.
translations.idiomatic: [decorum]; with guard of honor he went out at dawn and returned at night.

sentences.zh: 或幸天興宮，或游道會苑，陪侍之官，皆不堪命。

translations.literal: Sometimes he visited the Tianxing Palace or roamed Dao Assembly Park; the officials who accompanied him could not endure the strain.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he visited the Tianxing Palace or roamed Dao Assembly Park; the officials who accompanied him could not endure the strain.

sentences.zh: 散樂雜戲魚龍爛漫之伎，常在目前。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous music, mixed entertainments, and fish-dragon pageantry were constantly before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous music, mixed entertainments, and fish-dragon pageantry were constantly before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 好令京城少年為婦人服飾，入殿歌舞，與後宮觀之，以為喜樂。

translations.literal: He loved to have youths of the capital dress in women's clothes, enter the hall to sing and dance, and watch with the inner palace as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to have youths of the capital dress in women's clothes, enter the hall to sing and dance, and watch with the inner palace as entertainment.

sentences.zh: 擯斥近臣，多所猜忌。

translations.literal: He pushed away close ministers and was much given to suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed away close ministers and was much given to suspicion.

sentences.zh: 又吝於財，略無賜與。

translations.literal: He was also stingy with wealth and almost never gave rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was also stingy with wealth and almost never gave rewards.

sentences.zh: 恐羣臣規諫，不得行己之志，常遣左右密伺察之，動止所為，莫不鈔錄，小有乘違，輒加其罪。

translations.literal: Fearing that ministers would remonstrate and he could not carry out his wishes, he constantly sent attendants to spy on them in secret; their movements and actions were all copied down, and the slightest transgression brought punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that ministers would remonstrate and he could not carry out his wishes, he constantly sent attendants to spy on them in secret; their movements and actions were all copied down, and the slightest transgression brought punishment.

sentences.zh: 自公卿已下，皆被楚撻，其間誅戮黜免者，不可勝言。

translations.literal: From high officials downward all were beaten with the cudgel; among them those executed, beaten to death, dismissed, or removed cannot be fully told.
translations.idiomatic: From high officials downward all were beaten with the cudgel; among them those executed, beaten to death, dismissed, or removed cannot be fully told.

sentences.zh: 每笞捶人，皆以百二十為度，名曰天杖。

translations.literal: Whenever he beat people, one hundred and twenty strokes was the standard, called the Heaven Rod.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he beat people, one hundred and twenty strokes was the standard, called the Heaven Rod.

sentences.zh: 宮人內職亦如之。

translations.literal: Palace women and inner attendants were treated the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women and inner attendants were treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 后妃嬪御，雖被寵嬖，亦多被杖背。

translations.literal: Consorts, imperial concubines, and palace ladies, though favored, were also often beaten on the back.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts, imperial concubines, and palace ladies, though favored, were also often beaten on the back.

sentences.zh: 於是內外恐懼，人不自安，皆求苟免，莫有固志，重足累息，以逮於終。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were filled with fear; men did not feel secure and all sought merely to escape; none had firm resolve; walking on tiptoe and holding their breath, they reached the end.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon inside and outside were filled with fear; men did not feel secure and all sought merely to escape; none had firm resolve; walking on tiptoe and holding their breath, they reached the end.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：高祖識嗣子之非才，顧宗祏之至重，滯愛同於晉武，則哲異於宋宣。

translations.literal: The historian writes: High Ancestor knew the heir lacked talent yet regarded the ancestral temple as supremely weighty; lingering affection was like Jin Emperor Wu, but discernment differed from Song Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: High Ancestor knew the heir lacked talent yet regarded the ancestral temple as supremely weighty; lingering affection was like Jin Emperor Wu, but discernment differed from Song Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 但欲威之以檟楚，期之於懲肅，義方之教，豈若是乎。

translations.literal: He only wished to awe him with the birch rod and expect reform through stern discipline—was the teaching of upright principle really like this?
translations.idiomatic: He only wished to awe him with the birch rod and expect reform through stern discipline—was the teaching of upright principle really like this?

sentences.zh: 卒使昏虐君臨，姦回肆毒，善無小而必棄，惡無大而弗為。

translations.literal: In the end a benighted and cruel ruler held the throne; wicked men ran rampant; good, however small, was always cast aside; evil, however great, was never left undone.
translations.idiomatic: In the end a benighted and cruel ruler held the throne; wicked men ran rampant; good, however small, was always cast aside; evil, however great, was never left undone.

sentences.zh: 窮南山之簡，未足書其過；

translations.literal: Exhaust the bamboo of the Southern Mountains and it would not suffice to record his faults;
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the bamboo of the Southern Mountains and it would not suffice to record his faults;

sentences.zh: 盡東觀之筆，不能記其罪。

translations.literal: Use up all the brushes of the Eastern Pavilion and they could not record his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Use up all the brushes of the Eastern Pavilion and they could not record his crimes.

sentences.zh: 然猶獲全首領，及子而亡，幸哉。

translations.literal: Yet he still kept his head intact and died leaving a son—fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still kept his head intact and died leaving a son—fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
